Mined noise - best of 10,000 random rules on SPY

Statistical validation and engine analysis   1004 observations · 252 periods per year

Is the measured edge real, and is the backtest that measured it trustworthy?

Falsified

This tool falsifies; it cannot validate. It finds reasons to disbelieve a backtest, never reasons to believe one. The findings below are what the tests actually established. Nothing here says the strategy cannot work - only that this backtest does not show that it does.

Findings (3)

Critical Sharpe does not survive the selection-adjusted bar SELECT-DEFLATED-SHARPE-FAILS

Deflated Sharpe is 0.081 against 10000 trials. The observed per-period Sharpe of 0.0811 sits against an expected best-of-10000 under the null of 0.1253.

What to do: Reduce the trial count by fixing parameters on theoretical grounds, extend the sample, or test the strategy on genuinely fresh data. Nothing else recovers a failed deflation.
High Backtest is too short to support its claim given the trial count SELECT-INSUFFICIENT-LENGTH

4.0 years of data against a minimum backtest length of 14.9 years for 10000 trials at a target Sharpe of 1.0.

What to do: Extend the sample, or reduce the number of configurations examined.
Medium The edge does not survive being traded late ENGINE-EXECUTION-FRAGILE

Trading the same book one period later retains 58% of the Sharpe (1.42 to 0.82 annualised). An edge that depends on executing at the moment the signal is computed is an artifact of the backtest's timing assumptions rather than a property of the market, and no real book is filled that promptly.

What to do: Re-run the backtest with a realistic execution lag for the venue and report that as the headline result. If the edge only exists at zero delay, it is not an edge.

What could not be tested

  • Risk-free adjustment: none was supplied, so every Sharpe on this page is computed on total returns. That overstates the risk-adjusted result by the cash rate divided by the volatility, and it overstates it most for the least volatile series in any comparison. Ken French's RF is the intended source.
  • Factor attribution: no factor returns were supplied (Ken French FF5 plus momentum is the intended source).
  • Parameter-neighbourhood plateau: no parameter grid scores were supplied.

Headline

Every Sharpe ratio on this page is annualised to 252 periods unless the row says otherwise. No risk-free rate was supplied, so these are total-return Sharpes. They overstate the risk-adjusted result by roughly the cash rate divided by the volatility - which flatters the least volatile series in any comparison on this page.

MeasureValue95% interval
Annualised Sharpe (naive annualisation) 1.42 0.42 to 2.41
Autocorrelation-adjusted (Lo 2002) 1.42 0.42 to 2.42
Per-period Sharpe0.0894 0.0263 to 0.1520

The interval is a stationary bootstrap with a Politis-White block length of 1.0 over 2000 resamples - not the analytic standard error, which assumes away the serial dependence these returns have.

Lo's adjustment moves the annualisation factor from 15.87 to 15.91, raising the annualised Sharpe by 0.2%: these returns are negatively autocorrelated at short lags, so naive sqrt(q) annualisation was too harsh.

Caveat: annualising to 252 periods implies a sum over 251 lags, but 1004 observations can only speak to about 37; the adjustment assumes no dependence beyond that, and cannot rule out longer-horizon persistence.

How much of this was the path it took?

Maximum drawdown is an extreme-value statistic, and one realisation of it says much less than it appears to. These are the same returns resampled in blocks, so the distributions show how different the headline figures could plausibly have been on another draw of the same process.

StatisticRealised Resampled median5th to 95th percentile Realised percentile
Total return 139.91% 136.81% 39.91% to 306.71% 51%
Annualised Sharpe 1.42 1.40 0.60 to 2.25 52%
Maximum drawdown -15.99% -16.76% -27.28% to -10.90% 56%
Drawdown a matched random walk would expect -16.50% same drift and volatility IID normal, no fat tails 55%

Both comparisons understate, and in opposite ways. block resampling with a mean block of 1.0 periods cannot reassemble drawdowns that unfolded over much longer horizons, so the resampled distribution understates how deep a drawdown this strategy can produce. The matched random walk assumes IID normal returns, so it has neither volatility clustering nor fat tails and will also come out shallower than reality. A realised drawdown far outside both means the loss came from the order in which returns arrived, and neither baseline can recreate it.

Deflation runs on returns net of 3 bps, the upper end of realistic cost for US large-cap ETFs, so this figure sits slightly below the gross Sharpe in the headline. Trial-Sharpe dispersion measured from 10000 trial columns. Sharpe ratios in this table are per-period because that is the scale the Deflated Sharpe is defined on; scaling both sides would not change the comparison.

The two selection tests here answer different questions and can disagree. The Deflated Sharpe asks whether this result beats the best of 10000 draws from a no-edge null; the Harvey-Liu BHY haircut asks whether the t-statistic survives a false-discovery correction across 10000 tests. Both fail here: BHY takes the t-statistic to 0.00 and the Deflated Sharpe does not clear its bar either.

The trial count prices the configurations declared for this backtest. An effect taken from published work arrives with a search history of its own - the papers that found it, and the ones that were never written - and nothing in this report can see that. Read 10000 as a floor on the number of things that were tried, not as the number of things that were tried.

Simulated null: the observed result sits at the 40.5% percentile of 1500 replications (p = 0.595). Validity check: the simulation and the closed form disagree by -24.5% - trials were correlated, so the effective number of independent bets is below n_trials and the analytic Deflated Sharpe over-penalises.

The degradation slope is deliberately not reported as evidence, and neither is the in-sample-against-out-of-sample scatter that usually accompanies this chart. CSCV splits one fixed sample into complementary halves, so the two Sharpes sum to a constant: the scatter falls on a line of slope near -1 whatever the strategy does, and the apparent decay is an identity rather than a finding. The right-hand panel shows what the winner actually earns out of sample instead.

Robustness

TestResultReading
Annualised Sharpe, low / high volatility 0.34 / 2.02 same sign
Annualised Sharpe across 20 start dates 0.87 to 1.82 stable
Profit concentration vs a normal baseline 1.18x as expected
Annualised Sharpe dropping the best 1% / 5% of periods 0.96 / -0.50 from 1.42
Sign-flip randomisation p-value 0.001 signal informative
Matched-exposure random entry p-value 0.009 timing adds value

The post-drop Sharpe falls steeply for almost any strategy - removing the best 5% of periods from a Sharpe-1.42 series is expected to push it below zero, which is why the concentration ratio, not the post-drop Sharpe, is what this test actually reads. A ratio near 1.0 means the profit is no more concentrated than the Sharpe alone implies.

Engine analysis: can this backtest be trusted as an implementation?

Independent of whether the strategy makes money. A sound-looking number from an unsound implementation is the more dangerous of the two failures, because nothing in the return series betrays it.

CheckResultDetail
Reads the future? no none beyond 2 periods
Same input, same output? yes 3 calls compared
Is there a decision to examine? yes 145 changes over 1004 periods, 0.1% of it flat
Survives being traded a period late? 58.0% retained Sharpe 1.42 to 0.82 annualised
Universe complete over the sample? yes all 1 instruments

No dependence on data more than about 2 periods after the decision point. The strategy revises its position every 2 periods on average, and a leak shorter than that is overwritten before it reaches the book.

Trading cost and trading delay are different questions and fail independently. A monthly rotation across liquid funds can absorb hundreds of basis points in fees and still lose its entire edge to a single session of delay, because the signal was picking up a reversal that had already reverted by the time anyone could act on it.

Survivorship itself cannot be measured from a return series - a universe of survivors looks exactly like a universe, which is why the report asks for it to be declared. Inclusion timing is the part that is visible: an instrument added the day it listed was chosen in the knowledge that it would exist.

Universe: declared point-in-time - it was not assembled from present-day membership, so nothing entered it with hindsight. A single instrument, SPY, fixed before the search.
